The smoke from cigarettes with a modified cigarette blend, containing 100% extracted and reconstituted tobacco, has a lower benzo(a)pyren content than the smoke from cigarettes with an unmodified cigarette blend.
the smoke from the experimental cigarette contained 40% less benzo(a)pyrenes, 60% less phenolic compounds, 50% less nicotine, 30% less carbon monoxide, and was significantly less toxic.
1) the amount of smoke produced is reduced, 2) the amount of benzo(a)pyrenes and phenolics is reduced in the smoke, and 3) the taste of the smoke is improved.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new method of processing tobacco leaves and non-tobaccos which will result in a smoke which is free from the toxic and carcinogenic substances found in the smoke from ordinary cigarettes.
the development of a process for producing tobacco or non-tobacco leaf material of improved flavour, aroma and burning characteristics.

the development of a method to extract tobacco or tobacco substitutes, to add back non-toxic agents to the extracted leaf, and to manufacture a cigarette from such reconstituted leaf which has improved burning characteristics, flavour and aroma, and which contains less toxic materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the process of extraction and reconstitution of the tobacco leaf is a safe and effective means of reducing the toxic and carcinogenic substances in tobacco smoke.

the process of extracting tobacco and non-tobbacco leaves to almost pure celluloses, reconstituting them to original weight and then smoking them as a tobacco product, reduces benzo(a)pyrenes, phenolic compounds and other toxic and/or carcinogenic materials in the smoke.

, when the tobacco leaf has been subjected to a chemical extraction process, the resultant smoke from the smoking product contains reduced levels of benzo(a)pyrenes and phenolics, and the smoke has improved flavour and aroma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chemical agents added to the reconstituted leaf are non-toxic and that the chemical extractions remove unhealthy substances.
we can reduce the benzo(a)pyrenes and phenolics in tobacco smoke by using a tobacco extraction procedure.
the chemical extraction process reduces the benzo(a)pyrenes and phenolic content of tobacco and non- tobacco smoke.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an opportunity to significantly reduce the levels of toxicants in smoke by reducing the amount of nicotine in cigarettes.

the use of a chemical extraction process on tobacco leaves is not only a safe and efficient way of improving the smoking experience but also of reducing the levels of benzo(a)pyrenes and phenolics, two known harmful substances.
the use of tobacco-free nicotine pouches may be an effective alternative to smoking, especially in the context of smoking cessation.
